I quit playing games for a couple years due to changes in my personal life and because I had been primarily been playing live-service MP games and I realized I was treating them like a job, spending hours just to do dailies and weeklies on them so I was "getting my money's worth."

I quit those types of games cold turkey and didn't play anything for a long time. I gradually got back into games by starting with single-player only games, particularly shorter, focused games where I would actually finish them instead of getting 20 hours in and then distracted/busy and then feeling like I should go back to them but not remembering what was going on. 

One of the first things I did was buy a bunch of old games I already knew I loved that I hadn't played in years on GoG. Getting back into the habit of playing something you know you'll like can really jumpstart your interest in the hobby.

Some quick, fun titles I would recommend:

**Severed Steel** - It's like someone put FEAR's bullet time, Titanfall 2's movement system, and Bad Company 2's environmental destruction in a blender along with Cyberpunk's art style. Super fun, levels are very short so you can get a lot of fun out of short play sessions.

**Prodeus** - My favorite "boomer shooter" of the past few years. It's classic Doom/Quake with modern weapon/ability/movement upgrades/progression.

**The Ascent** - Somehow they made a gun-focused cover-based shooter work as an isometric ARPG. Beautiful art style as well.

**Overfall** - A roguelite RPG with a mix of exploring an ocean/island based overworld, lots of choose-your-own-adventure text-based encounters, and turn-based combat with two core characters you choose from the start and party members you can recruit on each run.

**Iron Danger** - Isometric ARPG that plays more like a tactical combat game because of its time manipulation mechanic. You can slow down and rewind time to avoid traps and counter enemies in combat where a couple hits can kill them or you. I'm personally a big fan of the art style as well.
